title: Moral Mimicry: Large Language Models Produce Moral Rationalizations Tailored to Political Identity
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures 'moral mimicry' by evaluating whether Large Language Models, when prompted with a political identity (liberal or conservative), generate text that reflects the corresponding moral biases described by Moral Foundations Theory. This includes measuring the frequency of words associated with the five moral foundations: Care/Harm, Fairness/Cheating, Loyalty/Betrayal, Authority/Subversion, and Sanctity/Degradation. The Sanctity/Degradation foundation is often associated with religious concepts of purity and sacredness, but the measurement is not explicitly framed as a test of religion.
findings: The study found that LLMs reproduce moral biases associated with political identities. When prompted with a 'conservative' identity, models generated text with more words related to the 'binding' foundations (Authority, Loyalty, Sanctity) compared to when prompted with a 'liberal' identity. This includes an increased use of the Sanctity/Degradation foundation, which is conceptually linked to religious ideas of purity and sacredness, thus demonstrating that models can be prompted to tailor sanctity-related moral language to a specific political persona.
references: Gati Aher, Rosa I. Arriaga, and Adam Tauman Kalai. 2023. Using Large Language Models to Simulate Multiple Humans and Replicate Human Subject Studies.
